content.page_summary: Discussion of revascularisation strategies in patients with spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD). CABG is recommended when dissection affects the left main or two proximal vessels, if PCI is not feasible or unsuccessful, and if there are symptoms/signs of ongoing myocardial ischaemia. Observational data note favourable early outcomes after CABG but a high (68%) rate of graft occlusion at 5 years. Vein grafts may be considered to preserve arterial conduits. Recommendation Table 11 provides technical recommendations for invasive strategies.
key_points: CABG recommended for SCAD when left main or two proximal vessels affected, or when PCI not feasible/unsuccessful, with ongoing ischaemia.
Small observational study: CABG in SCAD patients had favourable early clinical outcomes but 68% graft occlusion at 5 years.
Vein grafts should be considered to preserve arterial conduits due to risk of anastomosis failure and spontaneous healing restoring flow.
Recommendation Table 11 summarises technical aspects of invasive strategies.

recommendations.recommendation: Radial access is recommended as the standard approach, unless there are overriding procedural considerations.
PCI with stent deployment in the IRA during the index procedure is recommended in patients undergoing PPCI.
